newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fuji Heavy half-year profit up five-fold.
newsitem.headline: Fuji Heavy half-year profit up five-fold.

text.p: Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd, the maker of Subaru cars, said on Thursday its April-September parent current profit increased five-fold from its year-ago level to 11.45 billion yen.
The surge in profit was mainly due to the weaker yen and strong demand for Subaru cars abroad, the company said.
"Without a declining yen, we would not have posted gains," company vice president Takayoshi Yoshihashi told reporters.
The yen's weakening alone led to profit of nine billion yen profit in the six months. A rise of one yen in the dollar translated into profit of 500 million yen for the company.
The average dollar rate for the April-September period stood at 105 yen after 87 yen for the same period a year ago. Fuji sees the rate at 105 yen for the full business year.
Fuji Heavy, owned 4.2 percent by Nissan Motor Co Ltd, sees its profit for the full business year rising to 26 billion yen from 10.11 billion yen a year ago.
Exports of components for Fuji's overseas output rose 45 percent in the half year. Exports of cars jumped 53 percent.

The company raised its forecast for car exports in 1996/97 to 77,000 from its May forecast of 67,000. It also revised up its forecast for its export of knockdown kits to 106,000 from its earlier forecast of 105,000.

Sales by its aerospace division in the half-year rose to 25.65 billion yen from 22.90 billion yen a year ago on sales of components for the Boeing 777, and sales for the full year would rise to 59 billion yen from 55.1 billion yen a year ago, another company spokesman said.
Fuji Heavy supplies wings and main landing gear doors for Boeing 777, AH-1S anti-tank helicopters, and UH-1J utility helicopters for Japan's Defence Agency.
